title: Sell Mineral Rights in Dunbar, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Dunbar, PA | Fayette County
metaDescription: Dunbar sits near the historic Dunbar Furnace site in Fayette County. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly from owners, cash offer, no broker fee.
heroLead: Dunbar takes its name from one of Pennsylvania's earliest iron furnaces, and the mineral history in this corner of Fayette County runs through iron, coal, and coke long before any gas company arrived.
intro: The Dunbar Furnace site nearby is a reminder that this part of Fayette County had an industrial mineral economy going back to the 1700s, iron ore first, then coal and coke a century later. That layered history shows up in local deeds, which can reference several different mineral estates conveyed and reserved at different points, sometimes making a modern gas lease question depend on paperwork that's genuinely centuries old.
If your family has land or an inherited interest near Dunbar and the history feels like more than you can untangle alone, that's exactly what we do before making a cash offer.

sections.heading: Three Centuries of Mineral History on One Tract
paragraphs: It's not unusual for a Dunbar-area chain of title to include an iron-era conveyance, a later coal severance, and a modern oil and gas lease, each layered on top of the last. Figuring out what remains with the current surface owner versus what was carved away generations ago takes patient research through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds, and we do that work rather than asking you to.
This kind of layered history is part of why we never assume a Dunbar deed matches what a neighboring parcel's history looks like.

sections.heading: Flank Acreage With Selective Activity
paragraphs: This part of Fayette County sits on the edge of the Marcellus wet-gas fairway, which has meant operator interest here is more selective than in the deep-core counties to the west. Some Dunbar-area sections have seen leasing and even drilling, others haven't. We check current permitting for your specific tract before discussing any value.

sections.heading: A Small Interest From a Long-Gone Industry
paragraphs: A lot of what we buy near Dunbar is a small fractional interest that traces back to a family connection with the old iron or coal operations, not a large working farm. Those interests are often forgotten until an estate surfaces the paperwork. We're glad to review whatever you have and make a straightforward offer.

faqs.question: My family's Dunbar land has a history going back to the old iron furnace. Does that affect our mineral rights today?
faqs.answer: It can. Multiple historical severances, iron, coal, and later gas, sometimes layer on the same tract. We trace the full chain of title to see what remains with your family today.

faqs.question: Is Dunbar in an active Marcellus area?
faqs.answer: It sits on the flank of the wet-gas core, so activity is more selective. We check recent permitting near your specific tract before discussing value.

faqs.question: I only have a small interest tied to an old family connection to the mines. Is it worth anything?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. We regularly buy small, historically rooted fractional interests like this.
